{"user":"I’m taking a 6-day trip to Rome next month and want a compact plan. Can you suggest a day-by-day itinerary with the major sights, plus a couple of neighborhood options for where to eat each night? I don’t need tickets booked—just a schedule and some restaurant areas.","plus_response":"Absolutely—here’s a compact but well-paced 6-day Rome itinerary with major sights and nightly neighborhood options, and I’ll also add a few practical routing notes so you can move between areas efficiently.

Day 1 (Centro Storico + first highlights)
- Morning: Colosseum (area) + Roman Forum/Palatine viewpoint
- Lunch: Monti (easy walk from the Colosseum)
- Afternoon: Capitoline Hill + Piazza Venezia
- Evening: Trastevere (night atmosphere)

Day 2 (Vatican + surrounding art)
- Morning: Vatican Museums + Sistine Chapel
- Lunch: Prati
- Afternoon: St. Peter’s Basilica + Castel Sant’Angelo exterior/photo stops
- Evening: Borgo / Prati for dinner options

Day 3 (Pantheon to Trevi + classic center loop)
- Morning: Pantheon + Piazza Navona
- Lunch: Centro Storico side streets
- Afternoon: Trevi Fountain + Spanish Steps
- Evening: Campo de’ Fiori (lively walkability) or Monti

Day 4 (Ancient Rome beyond the obvious + sunset views)
- Morning: Baths of Caracalla (or Appian Way walk if you prefer)
- Lunch: San Giovanni (nearby)
- Afternoon: Aventine Hill + Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci)
- Evening: Testaccio (popular local-food neighborhood)

Day 5 (Borghese + neighborhoods)
- Morning: Galleria Borghese area (plan early)
- Lunch: Parioli
- Afternoon: Villa Borghese stroll + Pincio Terrace
- Evening: Monti (more dining variety than you’d expect) 

Day 6 (Old-school markets + one “choose your own” block)
- Morning: Campo de’ Fiori or Mercato area browsing (morning vibe)
- Lunch: Jewish Ghetto (quick, dense options)
- Afternoon (pick one): Castel Sant’Angelo interior OR a guided-style walk through the historic center by district
- Evening: Trastevere for a final dinner

Restaurant-neighborhood options (two each night, aligned to your schedule)
- Night 1: Trastevere + Monti
- Night 2: Prati + Borgo
- Night 3: Campo de’ Fiori + Centro Storico side streets (Pantheon/Piazza area)
- Night 4: Testaccio + San Giovanni
- Night 5: Monti + Parioli
- Night 6: Jewish Ghetto + Trastevere

If you tell me what time of day you prefer to start (early morning vs late start) and whether you’re more into art museums or archaeological sites, I can tighten the timing further and suggest 1–2 “fallback” stops per day so the schedule stays flexible if crowds are heavy.","minus_response":"Sure—here’s a compact 6-day Rome day-by-day outline with major sights, plus two neighborhood areas each night for where to eat.

Day 1: Colosseum + Roman Forum/Palatine (morning), Capitoline area (afternoon), Trastevere dinner.
- Dinner areas: Trastevere, Monti

Day 2: Vatican Museums/Sistine Chapel (morning), St. Peter’s (afternoon), Prati dinner.
- Dinner areas: Prati, Borgo

Day 3: Pantheon + Piazza Navona (morning), Trevi Fountain + Spanish Steps (afternoon), Campo de’ Fiori dinner.
- Dinner areas: Campo de’ Fiori, Centro Storico

Day 4: Baths of Caracalla or Appian Way walk (morning), Aventine Hill/Orange Garden (afternoon), Testaccio dinner.
- Dinner areas: Testaccio, San Giovanni

Day 5: Villa Borghese/Borghese area (morning), Borghese Park stroll + Pincio (afternoon), Monti dinner.
- Dinner areas: Monti, Parioli

Day 6: Jewish Ghetto/markets (morning), choose one: Castel Sant’Angelo OR another historic walk (afternoon), Trastevere final dinner.
- Dinner areas: Jewish Ghetto, Trastevere

If you want, you can pick one preferred start time (early vs late) and I can tell you how to shift each day’s order, but this should already give you a workable schedule and good neighborhood choices for evenings."}
